reason: The draft answers Marisol's question directly and honestly: no to doubling to 80 miles and no to running twice a day. It gives clear reasons. Going from 40 to 80 doubles her load in one step, and her club mate built up to 70 over a long time while she started this build at about 30. That's the most important call this week, and the draft gets it right. The plan adds up to 44 miles, a step of about 10% from 40 and still below her 53-mile week. It keeps her schedule: Monday and Friday off, the session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday. Her heavy legs cleared by Thursday, with no pain, so 7 mi at marathon pace (8:35–8:40, which matches a 3:45 goal) is reasonable. A 16 mi long run is plausible after a 53-mile week. Every day comes with a distance, a pace and a heart-rate cap, so it can be run as written. I took off a point because the draft states things the card doesn't support. "You followed last week's plan exactly" isn't on the card, and neither is the race date behind "five weeks". It also doesn't mention why she dropped from 53 to 40 miles, which affects how she should build from here.

Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"
